title: CDC vouchers and whether they push up the cost of living
asked: Mr Lee Hong Chuang asked whether giving CDC vouchers to every Singaporean household, regardless of socioeconomic status, worsens the cost of living through demand-pull inflation.
response: Mr Shawn Huang said there is no evidence the CDC Vouchers Scheme has worsened the cost of living through inflation, noting CPI-All items inflation fell from 4.8% in 2023 to 2.4% in 2024 and 0.9% in 2025 while the voucher quantum rose. Asked in a supplementary whether studies had been done on how far the vouchers help households, he said the Government regularly reviews scheme effectiveness, and that Assurance Package support grew from $6.6 billion in 2022 to more than $10 billion in 2025, fully offsetting expenditure increases for lower-income households and substantially offsetting them for middle-income households each year from 2022 to 2025. He also listed structural support for education, healthcare, housing and retirement, and targeted schemes for vulnerable groups.

key_points.point: No evidence that the CDC Vouchers Scheme has worsened the cost of living through inflation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: There is no evidence that the CDC Vouchers Scheme has worsened the cost-of-living due to inflation.

key_points.point: The Government regularly reviews how effective its schemes are at helping Singaporeans with cost of living concerns.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The Government regularly reviews the effectiveness of our schemes to ensure that they continue to help Singaporeans manage cost of living concerns.

key_points.point: Assurance Package support was raised from an initial $6.6 billion in 2022 to more than $10 billion in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: we actually increased the support delivered via the AP from an initial $6.6 billion in 2022 to more than $10 billion in 2025

key_points.point: These enhancements fully offset expenditure increases from high inflation for lower-income households and substantially offset them for middle-income households each year from 2022 to 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: These enhancements have fully offset the expenditure increases arising from high inflation for lower-income households and substantially offset the expenditure increases for middle-income households each year from 2022 to 2025.

key_points.point: Structural support covers education, healthcare, housing and retirement, with targeted schemes such as Workfare Income Supplement, Fresh Start Housing and Silver Support.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme for lower-wage workers, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme for lower-income families and the Silver Support Scheme for seniors who had low incomes in their working years
